cards.text: Jesus takes the Twelve aside, just His disciples. He says, "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem," and He's got more to say. Friend, when anybody pulls you aside and starts with "Look," you put your cookie DOWN.

cards.question: Jesus calls Himself the Son of Man. He says everything the ___ have written about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them what's coming for the Son of Man, and baker, it is not a parade. First, He will be delivered over.

cards.question: Jesus says the Son of Man will be delivered over. To whom?
Jesus says the Son of Man will be mocked, insulted and spit upon.

cards.text: It gets heavier. Jesus says they will flog Him and kill Him, but He isn't done talking yet.

cards.question: Jesus says the Son of Man will be killed. What does He say happens on the third day?
The disciples understand what Jesus just told them about Jerusalem.

cards.text: They don't get any of it; the meaning was hidden from them. Friend, I lay face down on a blender manual in that junk drawer for YEARS, and I still couldn't tell you how a blender works.
Now Jesus is getting close to Jericho. There's a man sitting beside the road, and he's blind.

cards.question: The blind man sits beside the road near Jericho, ___.

cards.text: He can't see the crowd going by, but he can sure HEAR it. So he asks what's happening.

cards.question: The blind man asks what all the noise is about. What does the crowd tell him?

answers.text: Jesus of Nazareth is passing by
A wedding party is passing by

cards.text: Friend, this man does not leave a voicemail and hope somebody calls back. He calls out to Jesus, and he calls Him the Son of David.

cards.question: The blind man calls out to Jesus, the Son of David. What does he ask Him for?

cards.text: The people leading the way are not having it. They tell him to be silent.

cards.question: When the people leading the way tell the blind man to be silent, he goes quiet.

cards.text: Tell this man to hush and he cries out all the LOUDER. Mags would hire him on the spot.

cards.question: The blind man won't stop calling out to Jesus. What does Jesus do?

answers.text: Stops and has him brought over
Sends the crowd to quiet him
Calls back to him and keeps walking

cards.text: The folks leading the way wanted this man SILENT. Now he's standing near Jesus, and Jesus is asking HIM a question.

cards.question: Jesus asks the blind man a question. What is it?

answers.text: What do you want Me to do for you
Why are you shouting at Me

cards.text: The man calls Him Lord and asks to see again. No waiting room, no paperwork, Jesus just says, "Receive your sight!"

cards.question: Jesus tells the man it's his ___ that has healed him.

cards.text: And immediately, the man can see. Not in six to eight business days, friend, IMMEDIATELY!

cards.question: The man near Jericho can see again. What does he do next?

answers.text: Follows Jesus and gives God the glory
Goes home and tells his family
Runs into Jericho to tell the town

cards.question: When all the people see the blind man healed, they give praise to God.

findings.problem: Too many of this stop's choices depend on luck rather than reasoning from the setup. Card 4 gives no basis for choosing the Gentiles, card 7 gives no basis for knowing what happens on the third day, and card 8 gives no indication that the disciples fail to understand. Thus at least three of the stop's five choices are discovery questions, so they dominate the stop instead of remaining occasional exceptions.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The first sentence retells the leaders' demand for silence from Luke 18:39, while the second uses Luke 18:40. Citing only Luke 18:40 is too narrow; the card uses Luke 18:39-40.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The question identifies the person only as "the man," leaving it dependent on the preceding, no-longer-visible story card. It should identify him as the blind man near Jericho so the question stands on its own.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.
